newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to use option to buy China, Vietnam rice.
newsitem.headline: Manila to use option to buy China, Vietnam rice.

text.p: The state-owned National Food Authority will use its option to buy an additional 100,000 tonnes of rice from Vietnam and another 50,000 tonnes from China to complete its procurement programme before July this year, an Agriculture Department official said on Thursday.
"NFA is just waiting for the signature of Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero before it confirm the order to the respective countries," the official who requested not to be named told Reuters.
The official said Escudero had approved the proposal to import additional rice from Vietnam and China on top of those previously contracted.
President Fidel Ramos has authorised the NFA to import up to 650,000 tonnes of rice from neighbouring countries to beef up the country's buffer stocks before July this year.
Philippine rice harvests in the third quarter are traditionally low.
The NFA has so far bought 205,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand at $300 per tonne C&F, and 100,000 tonnes each from Vietnam, China and Malaysia at $291.50 per tonne C&F.
The contract clinched by Vietnam, China and Malaysia all carried an option for the NFA to buy additional 100,000 tonnes each.
